title: The facts on quantum self-dual Einstein gravity and self-dual Yang-Mills theory
summary:
Self-dual Einstein gravity is a one-loop exact, UV and IR finite, diffeomorphism invariant, non-unitary theory of quantum gravity in four dimensions. The only non-trivial amplitudes are the one-loop-all-plus amplitudes, and they are equal to those of pure Einstein gravity.
  In these notes we review SDG and SDYM pedagogically. We walk the reader through key calculations, fill in some gaps in the literature, and point out directions for future research. Topics include: derivation of the self-dual actions from the full Einstein gravity/YM actions in lightcone gauge, decoupling of ghosts, Berends-Giele currents, vanishing of tree-level-one-minus amplitudes, celestial $Lw_{1+\infty}$ symmetry, perturbiners, double-off-shell current calculation of one-loop-all-plus SDYM and SDG amplitudes, dimension shifting, unitarity cuts, the BDPR gravity formula, one-loop color ordering, and the covariant formulations of the self-dual theories as well as their their gauge fixing. We also review some selected results from the celestial holography program, and briefly comment on an all-n expression for the one-loop-one-minus gravity amplitudes.

AI.tldr: This paper provides a pedagogical review of self-dual gravity (SDG) and self-dual Yang-Mills (SDYM) theories in four dimensions, covering key calculations, derivations, and selected results from celestial holography.
AI.motivation: Self-dual Einstein gravity is a remarkable theory—one-loop exact, UV and IR finite, diffeomorphism invariant, and non-unitary—whose only non-trivial amplitudes are the one-loop-all-plus amplitudes, matching those of pure Einstein gravity. The authors aim to fill gaps in the existing literature and provide a comprehensive pedagogical resource for researchers.
AI.method: The review covers: derivation of self-dual actions from full Einstein gravity/YM in lightcone gauge, ghost decoupling, Berends-Giele currents, vanishing of tree-level-one-minus amplitudes, celestial Lw_{1+∞} symmetry, perturbiners, double-off-shell current calculations of one-loop-all-plus amplitudes, dimension shifting, unitarity cuts, the BDPR gravity formula, one-loop color ordering, and covariant formulations with gauge fixing.
AI.result: The paper systematically walks through key calculations for SDG and SDYM, filling gaps in the literature, and reviews selected celestial holography results as well as an all-n expression for one-loop-one-minus gravity amplitudes.
AI.conclusion: The review consolidates the understanding of self-dual theories as tractable quantum gravity models with special amplitude properties, while pointing out open directions for future research.

title: Renormalization in Liouville gravity and stochastic inflation
summary: Motivated by inflation and Liouville theory, we consider random $d$-dimensional geometries characterized by an overall scale factor $ds^2 = e^{2 ζ} dx^2 $ given in terms of a random Gaussian field $ζ(x)$ with logarithmic correlations. We discuss aspects of the renormalization of the volume element $e^{d ζ}$, connecting well-known Liouville theory formulas (KPZ) and inflationary ones. By starting from a fixed physical cutoff and coarse-graining operators to a fixed fiducial cutoff, defined via the flat metric $dx^2$, we provide a direct physical derivation of the KPZ scaling relation. We point out that the same renormalization problem arises in stochastic inflation, where it is modeled by Brownian motion of the inflaton field. We show that the breakdown of the renormalization of the Liouville volume when the fluctuation amplitude exceeds a critical value corresponds to the transition to eternal inflation. In $d = 2$, this matches the familiar $c_m = 1$ barrier in Liouville gravity. We also discuss connections to mathematical probabilistic approaches to random surfaces.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes random d-dimensional geometries with scale factor driven by a log-correlated Gaussian field, deriving the KPZ scaling relation via a direct physical renormalization approach, and connecting the breakdown of Liouville volume renormalization to the eternal inflation transition (matching the c_m=1 barrier in d=2 Liouville gravity).
AI.motivation: The authors aim to unify two seemingly distinct frameworks—inflationary physics and Liouville theory—by recognizing they share the same underlying renormalization problem for random geometries with log-correlated fields, thereby providing a bridge between KPZ scaling in Liouville gravity and stochastic inflation dynamics.
AI.method: Starting from a fixed physical cutoff and coarse-graining operators to a fixed fiducial cutoff (defined via the flat metric), the authors provide a direct physical derivation of the KPZ scaling relation. They then map the same renormalization problem to stochastic inflation (modeled as Brownian motion of the inflaton field) and analyze the critical fluctuation amplitude where volume renormalization breaks down.
AI.result: The authors show that the breakdown of Liouville volume renormalization at a critical fluctuation amplitude corresponds to the transition to eternal inflation. In d=2, this matches the familiar c_m=1 barrier in Liouville gravity. Connections to mathematical probabilistic approaches to random surfaces are also discussed.
AI.conclusion: The paper establishes a concrete physical and mathematical bridge between Liouville theory (KPZ scaling) and stochastic inflation, identifying the eternal inflation transition as the same critical phenomenon as the c_m=1 barrier in Liouville gravity, with implications for random surface theory.

title: Positivity in energy correlators and the event distribution formula
summary: Energy correlators are universal observables, well defined across a wide range of theories and spacetime dimensions, from gauge theory and conformal field theory to string theory. Energy correlators are constrained by three fundamental properties: pointwise positivity of the energy flux, global positivity originating from their interpretation as state norms in a unitary theory, and energy conservation organizing multi-point energy correlators into an infinite consistent hierarchy. We argue that the most general solution to the infinite hierarchy positivity problem of energy correlators is given by the event distribution formula, which expresses energy correlators as moments of the measure on the space of probability measures on the celestial sphere. We work out in detail implications of positivity for two- and three-point energy correlators and show that it implies nontrivial two-sided bounds on their multipole expansion coefficients. The bounds obtained by requiring consistency of the infinite hierarchy of energy correlators are strictly stronger than those obtained by imposing positivity of the two- and three-point correlators alone. For the low-spin multipole coefficients studied in the paper, the derived bounds are optimal in the sense that their extrema are realized by finite mixtures of finite-particle events. We further demonstrate consequences of positivity in energy correlators in collider physics and conformal field theories.

AI.tldr: The paper derives the most general positivity constraints on energy correlators, showing they take the form of a moment problem on the space of probability measures on the celestial sphere. The resulting bounds on multipole expansion coefficients are strictly stronger than pointwise positivity alone and are optimal, with extrema realized by finite mixtures of finite-particle events.
AI.motivation: Energy correlators are fundamental universal observables constrained by positivity and energy conservation, but the full implications of the infinite hierarchy of consistency conditions had not been systematically understood. The authors aim to derive the most general mathematical structure governing these constraints.
AI.method: The paper formulates the positivity problem of energy correlators as an infinite hierarchy moment problem on the space of probability measures on the celestial sphere. They prove that the general solution is given by the event distribution formula (mixtures of point configurations), and derive two-sided bounds on two- and three-point multipole expansion coefficients by imposing consistency across the full hierarchy.
AI.result: The derived hierarchy bounds are strictly stronger than imposing pointwise positivity on two- and three-point correlators alone. For low-spin multipole coefficients, the bounds are proven optimal, with extrema realized by finite mixtures of finite-particle events.
AI.conclusion: The infinite hierarchy of energy correlator positivity implies tight, optimal bounds on multipole moments that have concrete consequences in both collider physics and conformal field theory applications.

title: Why Cooper pairs live in AdS2: a spectral analysis of the Yukawa-SYK model
summary: We establish the spectral foundation of the geometric formulation of Cooper pairing in the Yukawa--Sachdev--Ye--Kitaev model. Starting from the large-$N$ bilocal effective action, we derive the Gaussian fluctuation kernel in the even-frequency spin-singlet Cooper channel. Following the construction of Maldacena and Stanford, we determine the kernel eigenvalue $k\left(h\right)$ analytically for arbitrary conformal weight $h$ and resolve the pairing fluctuations into the continuous and discrete sectors of the associated de-Sitter space Laplacian. We show that the superconducting instability and the universal low-energy fluctuations near it reside entirely in the continuous scattering sector, while the discrete modes remain non-critical. Expanding the kernel about the lowest continuum mode yields a Klein--Gordon action on ${\rm dS}_2$, restricted to the continuous spectral subspace. This is precisely the subspace on which the inverse Radon transform to ${\rm AdS}_2$ is well defined. The projected bilocal Cooper-pair field can therefore be mapped onto a scalar matter field propagating in ${\rm AdS}_2$, without requiring any further spectral restriction on the bulk theory. Our results provide the missing microscopic justification for the projection implicit in earlier holographic formulations and clarify how a local bulk field emerges from the bilocal pairing theory.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes the spectral foundations of geometric Cooper pairing in the Yukawa-SYK model by deriving the Gaussian fluctuation kernel in the Cooper channel analytically, showing that superconducting instability resides in the continuous scattering sector of the de Sitter Laplacian, and proving that the projected bilocal Cooper-pair field maps onto a scalar matter field in AdS₂ without additional spectral restrictions.
AI.motivation: The authors aim to provide a microscopic justification for the projection implicit in earlier holographic formulations of Cooper pairing, clarifying how a local bulk field emerges from the bilocal pairing theory in the Yukawa-SYK model.
AI.method: Starting from the large-N bilocal effective action, the kernel eigenvalue k(h) is derived analytically for arbitrary conformal weight h following the Maldacena-Stanford construction. Pairing fluctuations are decomposed into continuous and discrete sectors of the de Sitter space Laplacian, and the kernel is expanded about the lowest continuum mode to yield a Klein-Gordon action on dS₂ restricted to the continuous spectral subspace.
AI.result: The superconducting instability and universal low-energy fluctuations reside entirely in the continuous scattering sector while discrete modes remain non-critical. The continuous spectral subspace is exactly where the inverse Radon transform to AdS₂ is well defined, enabling a direct mapping of the projected bilocal Cooper-pair field onto a scalar matter field in AdS₂ without further spectral restrictions.
AI.conclusion: The results provide the missing microscopic foundation for prior holographic projections, demonstrating that a local bulk field in AdS₂ emerges naturally from the bilocal Cooper-pairing theory in the Yukawa-SYK model.

title: Classical and Hybrid Quantum Machine Learning for Trigger-Like Event Selection on CMS Open Data: An Eight-Qubit, PCA-Constrained Benchmark
summary: Event triggering sits at the heart of high-energy physics, where the rare events of interest must be retained while an overwhelming background is discarded under tight latency and bandwidth budgets. This work compares four classical machine learning models, namely a support vector machine, an artificial neural network, a convolutional network and a long short-term memory network, with four hybrid quantum counterparts, on a trigger-like binary classification task built from CMS open data. The label is defined by an invariant-mass window, and the inputs combine reconstructed kinematics with physics-motivated derived variables: the pseudorapidity difference, the wrapped azimuthal difference, the angular separation and the total transverse momentum. The quantum models run under a fixed resource budget of eight qubits, a principal-component compression to sixteen features and state-vector simulation. Every model shares the same stratified split, the same preprocessing and a common decision threshold, and performance is reported through accuracy, ROC-AUC, F1-score, precision and recall. The strongest classical model is the artificial neural network, at 93.53 percent accuracy and 0.9819 ROC-AUC, while the strongest quantum model is the quantum convolutional network, at 90.89 percent accuracy and 0.9731 ROC-AUC, with the quantum neural network close behind. The quantum-kernel and recurrent quantum approaches trail both, which places the trainable hybrid embeddings ahead within this budget. The study is meant as a controlled reference point rather than a claim of quantum advantage.

AI.tldr: This paper benchmarks four classical ML models (SVM, ANN, CNN, LSTM) against four hybrid quantum counterparts on a CMS open-data trigger-like binary classification task, under a fixed eight-qubit budget. The classical ANN leads at 93.53% accuracy / 0.9819 ROC-AUC, while the quantum convolutional network leads the quantum models at 90.89% / 0.9731, framed as a controlled reference point rather than evidence of quantum advantage.
AI.motivation: Event triggering in high-energy physics requires fast, accurate discrimination of rare signal events from overwhelming background under tight latency and bandwidth constraints. The authors aim to provide a controlled, apples-to-apples comparison of classical and hybrid quantum ML approaches for such trigger-like classification, where existing work tends to lack standardized benchmarks.
AI.method: The task is binary classification on CMS open data with a label defined by an invariant-mass window. Features combine reconstructed kinematics with derived physics variables (pseudorapidity difference, wrapped azimuthal difference, angular separation, total transverse momentum). All models share a stratified split, the same preprocessing and a common decision threshold. Classical models are SVM, ANN, CNN, LSTM; quantum models are their hybrid counterparts, constrained to eight qubits, PCA compression to sixteen features, and state-vector simulation. Performance is evaluated via accuracy, ROC-AUC, F1-score, precision, and recall.
AI.result: The ANN is the strongest classical model (93.53% accuracy, 0.9819 ROC-AUC). Among quantum models, the quantum convolutional network performs best (90.89% accuracy, 0.9731 ROC-AUC), with the quantum neural network close behind. Quantum-kernel and recurrent quantum approaches lag both, indicating that trainable hybrid embeddings are superior within the eight-qubit budget.
AI.conclusion: Trainable hybrid quantum embeddings, particularly the quantum convolutional network, close the gap to classical performance under a constrained quantum resource budget, but do not surpass the best classical model. The study serves as a controlled reference point for future work, not a demonstration of quantum advantage.

title: Inner products and closed universes
summary: We study overlaps of late-time states in semiclassical de Sitter quantum gravity. In a family of deformations of de Sitter JT gravity, we compute the no-boundary wavefunction to one-loop and derive the ultralocal late-time measure. The one-universe contribution to the norm is exactly eight times the sphere amplitude, so the pairing used by the Lorentzian measure differs from that implicit in Euclidean gravity. After summing over disconnected final universes, the no-boundary norm exponentiates the one-universe result, giving $\langle \!\langle \text{HH}|\text{HH}\rangle\!\rangle \approx \exp(8Z_{\rm sphere})$ rather than the sum over closed geometries, $Z_{\rm closed}\approx \exp(Z_{\rm sphere})$. We also review an analogous mismatch in Einstein gravity with positive cosmological constant, where the late-time no-boundary norm vanishes at one-loop, differing from the Euclidean sphere amplitude. We discuss the implications for cutting and gluing in perturbative gravity, and features that arise when extending this construction to sums over topologies.

AI.tldr: The paper studies late-time state overlaps in semiclassical de Sitter quantum gravity using a family of deformations of de Sitter JT gravity. Computing the no-boundary wavefunction to one-loop, the authors find the one-universe norm is exactly eight times the sphere amplitude, leading to an exponentiation of the no-boundary norm as exp(8Z_sphere) rather than the standard closed-geometry sum exp(Z_sphere). They also review a similar mismatch in Einstein gravity with positive cosmological constant and discuss implications for cutting/gluing in perturbative gravity and sums over topologies.
AI.motivation: To understand how late-time states (overlaps of Hartle-Hawking states) behave in semiclassical de Sitter quantum gravity, and to determine whether the Lorentzian pairing of states matches the Euclidean gravitational path integral measure.
AI.method: The authors compute the no-boundary wavefunction to one-loop order in a family of deformations of de Sitter JT gravity, derive the ultralocal late-time measure, and analyze the one-universe contribution to the norm. They compare this with the Euclidean sphere amplitude and then sum over disconnected final universes to obtain the exponentiated result. They additionally review an analogous calculation in Einstein gravity with positive cosmological constant.
AI.result: The one-universe contribution to the no-boundary norm is exactly eight times the sphere amplitude. Summing over disconnected final universes gives ⟨HH|HH⟩ ≈ exp(8Z_sphere), which differs from the closed-geometry sum exp(Z_sphere). In Einstein gravity with positive cosmological constant, the late-time no-boundary norm vanishes at one-loop, again differing from the Euclidean sphere amplitude. These reveal a mismatch between Lorentzian measure pairings and Euclidean gravity.
AI.conclusion: The Lorentzian measure used for late-time states differs from the implicit pairing in Euclidean gravity, with observable consequences for the norm of the no-boundary state. This has implications for cutting and gluing prescriptions in perturbative quantum gravity and for constructions that involve sums over spacetime topologies.

title: FlaSR: A Mathematica Package for the Automatic Generation of $U$-spin Sum Rules
summary: We present FlaSR, a Mathematica package for the automatic generation of higher-order amplitude and amplitude-squared $SU(2)$ flavor sum rules, with a particular emphasis on $U$-spin. The package is based on recent insights into the mathematical structure of flavor sum rules. Given a system of symmetry-related processes defined by a list of particle multiplets in the initial and final states, together with the transformation properties of the symmetry-limit Hamiltonian, the package generates the full list of processes and outputs amplitude and amplitude-squared sum rules for the system. For amplitude sum rules, the package generates the complete set at all orders in symmetry breaking for which such relations exist. For amplitude-squared sum rules, which translate directly into sum rules among physical observables, the current version of the package is not guaranteed to generate the complete set. We illustrate the scope of the package with a range of representative examples.

AI.tldr: FlaSR is a Mathematica package that automatically generates higher-order amplitude and amplitude-squared SU(2) flavor sum rules, with emphasis on U-spin. It generates complete sets of amplitude sum rules at all orders of symmetry breaking where such relations exist, and produces amplitude-squared sum rules for physical observables.
AI.motivation: Flavor sum rules are important theoretical tools for analyzing symmetry-related processes, but deriving them manually at higher orders becomes increasingly complex and error-prone. The authors aim to automate this process, particularly for SU(2) flavor symmetries like U-spin, where recent mathematical insights have clarified the underlying structure.
AI.method: The package takes as input a system of symmetry-related processes specified by initial and final state particle multiplets, along with the transformation properties of the symmetry-limit Hamiltonian. It then systematically generates all symmetry-related processes and derives amplitude and amplitude-squared sum rules using the mathematical structure of flavor sum rules.
AI.result: FlaSR generates complete sets of amplitude sum rules at all orders of symmetry breaking where such relations exist. For amplitude-squared sum rules (which correspond directly to physical observable relations), the package generates them but does not guarantee completeness in the current version. The paper demonstrates the package's capabilities with representative examples.
AI.conclusion: FlaSR provides an automated tool for generating flavor sum rules in SU(2) symmetry contexts, significantly streamlining the derivation process. While amplitude sum rules are generated completely, amplitude-squared sum rules may require further development to guarantee completeness.

title: Contact Structure-induced Symplectic Nearly Half-Flat $SU(3)$ Structure in Finite-$N$ Thermal ${\cal M}$-Theory
summary: The ${\cal M}$-theory dual of thermal QCD-like theories constructed in arXiv:1306.4339, 2004.07259 involves, as shown in arXiv:2211.13186, a closed $G_2$-structure seven-fold $\mathcal{M}_7$ supporting Contact 3-Structures (C3S) that induce a ``transverse'' $SU(3)$-structure. We prove that this induced structure belongs to the symplectic nearly half-flat (S(nearly)HF) class: $dω_Φ=0$ exactly, while $dΩ_+$ is suppressed as $\mathcal{O}(e^{-N^{1/3}/\mathcal{O}(1)})$ in the infrared "MQGP limit", leaving $W_Φ^{SU(3)}=W_2^-$ as the sole non-vanishing Chiossi--Salamon torsion class and completing the $G$-structure classification of the MQGP dual initiated in arXiv:1507.02692,2004.07259, 2211.13186. As a physical application, Kaluza--Klein reduction of the eleven-dimensional Hodge dual of the differential of the $G_2$-structure positive three-form on $\mathcal{M}_7$, organised through the $G_2$/S(nearly)HF torsion data, yields a radial ``magnetic field'' $\mathcal{B}_{\rm KK}(r)$ whose squared norm factorises exactly into external and internal factors. $\mathcal{B}_{\rm KK}(r)$ satisfies a Bessel-type ODE with a regular singular point at the horizon; normalisability and infrared regularity select $J_2$, with harmonicity of the aforementioned internal factor recovered from the large-$N$ suppression. $\mathcal{B}_{\rm KK}$ is related to the magnetic field of the type~IIA flavour $D6$-branes via a non-linear power law, furnishing a top-down holographic mechanism for generating weak magnetic fields in finite-temperature string theory.

AI.tldr: This paper proves that the transverse SU(3)-structure induced by the closed G2-structure on the seven-fold M7 in the MQGP (M-theory QGP) dual of thermal QCD belongs to the symplectic nearly half-flat (S(nearly)HF) class, with W2- as the sole non-vanishing Chiossi-Salamon torsion class. As a physical application, KK reduction yields a radial magnetic field satisfying a Bessel-type ODE, which is related to type IIA flavour D6-brane magnetic fields via a non-linear power law.
AI.motivation: To complete the G-structure classification of the MQGP dual of thermal QCD-like theories initiated in earlier works, and to derive a top-down holographic mechanism for generating weak magnetic fields in finite-temperature string theory from the torsion data of the G2/S(nearly)HF structure.
AI.method: The authors analyze the closed G2-structure on M7 supporting Contact 3-Structures (C3S) that induce a transverse SU(3)-structure. They prove the induced structure lies in the symplectic nearly half-flat class by showing dωΦ=0 exactly and dΩ+ is exponentially suppressed in the infrared MQGP limit, leaving W2- as the sole non-vanishing torsion class. They then perform KK reduction of the eleven-dimensional Hodge dual of the differential of the positive three-form, organized through the torsion data, to derive a radial magnetic field B_KK(r) satisfying a Bessel-type ODE, with normalizability and IR regularity selecting the J2 Bessel function.
AI.result: The transverse SU(3)-structure is proven to be S(nearly)HF, completing the G-structure classification. KK reduction yields B_KK(r) with squared norm factorising into external and internal factors, satisfying a Bessel-type ODE with regular singular point at the horizon. J2 is selected by physical constraints, and B_KK relates to type IIA flavour D6-brane magnetic fields via a non-linear power law, providing a holographic mechanism for weak magnetic field generation.
AI.conclusion: The paper completes the torsion classification of the MQGP dual and establishes a top-down holographic connection between G2-structure torsion data and weak magnetic field generation in finite-temperature strongly coupled gauge theories.

title: OperatorToC++: Transpiling Matched EFT Coefficients to Low-Level Routines
summary: In recent years, significant progress has been made in the development of automated tools that match the parameters of new physics models and the appropriate low-energy Effective Field Theories. This work introduces an extensible, hybrid tool, OperatorToC++, that combines the strengths of Mathematica and C++ to facilitate the next steps beyond the matching. OperatorToC++ efficiently tackles the complexities within the analytical matched expressions such as intricate loop-functions and lengthy sums and products involving tensor objects. It then translates and bundles the results into C++ classes and functions which provide a convenient platform for further numerical analyses. Finally, it offers the possibility of calling the compiled Wilson coefficient methods as Python functions, thus enabling to link them with the vast Python library ecosystem for High Energy Physics workflows.

AI.tldr: OperatorToC++ is a hybrid tool combining Mathematica and C++ to automatically translate matched Effective Field Theory expressions into C++ classes and Python-callable functions for numerical analysis.
AI.motivation: Automated matching between new physics models and low-energy Effective Field Theories has advanced significantly, but the next steps beyond matching—handling complex analytical expressions such as loop-functions and tensor sums/products—remain challenging and require an efficient tool to bridge the gap between analytical results and numerical analysis.
AI.method: OperatorToC++ combines Mathematica for symbolic computation and C++ for efficient numerical evaluation. It processes intricate loop-functions and lengthy sums/products involving tensor objects in the matched analytical expressions, translates them into C++ classes and functions, and provides Python bindings for the compiled Wilson coefficient methods.
AI.result: The tool successfully tackles the complexity of analytical matched expressions, bundles results into C++ classes and functions, and enables calling compiled Wilson coefficient methods as Python functions for integration with the High Energy Physics Python ecosystem.
AI.conclusion: OperatorToC++ provides an extensible, hybrid solution that streamlines the transition from analytical EFT matching results to practical numerical implementations, offering flexibility through both C++ and Python interfaces for the High Energy Physics community.

title: Gravitational Compton Amplitude to All Orders in Perturbation Theory
summary: We show how amplitudes from the scattering of gravitational waves off compact objects in worldline effective field theory can be efficiently computed to arbitrary order in Newton's constant $G$. Our approach solves an effective wave equation for the partial-wave amplitude in which Wilson coefficients (tidal Love numbers) enter through boundary conditions at short distances. We then perform the sum over partial waves to obtain the momentum-space Compton amplitude in terms of elliptic polylogarithms. We reproduce recent results through $\mathcal{O}(G^4)$ and obtain new predictions up to $\mathcal{O}(G^7)$, with Love numbers first contributing at $\mathcal{O}(G^5)$. We find the first ultraviolet divergence in a classical gravitational amplitude at $\mathcal{O}(G^7)$, showing that a pure point-particle description is not consistent in general relativity. Matching to black hole perturbation theory, we show that static Love numbers vanish on-shell and predict subleading non-zero Schwarzschild black hole Love numbers.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a novel method to compute gravitational wave scattering amplitudes off compact objects using worldline effective field theory, solving an effective wave equation for partial-wave amplitudes with Wilson coefficients (tidal Love numbers) entering via boundary conditions. The approach reproduces known results through O(G⁴), provides new predictions up to O(G⁷), and discovers the first ultraviolet divergence in classical gravitational amplitudes at O(G⁷), indicating a pure point-particle description is inconsistent in general relativity.
AI.motivation: To develop an efficient computational framework for gravitational wave scattering amplitudes in worldline effective field theory that can be extended to arbitrary orders in Newton's constant G, overcoming limitations of existing perturbative approaches while probing the consistency of point-particle descriptions in general relativity.
AI.method: The authors formulate an effective wave equation for partial-wave amplitudes in worldline EFT, where Wilson coefficients (tidal Love numbers) appear as boundary conditions at short distances. They sum over partial waves to express the momentum-space Compton amplitude using elliptic polylogarithms.
AI.result: The method reproduces known results through O(G⁴), delivers new predictions up to O(G⁷), with Love numbers contributing from O(G⁵). The first UV divergence in a classical gravitational amplitude emerges at O(G⁷), and matching to black hole perturbation theory shows static Love numbers vanish on-shell while predicting subleading non-zero Schwarzschild black hole Love numbers.
AI.conclusion: The pure point-particle effective theory breaks down at O(G⁷) in general relativity due to a UV divergence, requiring corrections from black hole physics. The framework also resolves the Love number question by showing static Love numbers vanish on-shell while subleading non-zero Love numbers exist for Schwarzschild black holes.

title: First-Principles Nuclear Modeling for Light Dark Matter Experiments at the Intensity Frontier
summary: Accelerator-based experiments at the intensity frontier, in which a high-energy beam impinges on a nuclear target, serve as powerful probes of the light dark matter paradigm. Such experiments require precise modeling of the target nucleus for reliable signal predictions. We present the application of a many-body ab initio method to calculate light dark matter mediator production signal rates at electron fixed-target experiments, using chiral effective field theory interactions. Considering both elastic and quasi elastic scattering, we compute cross sections using a Monte Carlo event generator implementation informed by ab initio nuclear elastic form factors and spectral functions for three representative nuclei, $^{20}$Ne, $^{34}$Si, and $^{56}$Fe, at varying electron beam energies. We compare our results to a commonly used phenomenological parameterization, finding an increased signal yield by up to two orders of magnitude with our quasi elastic treatment and an agreement for lighter mediators.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a many-body ab initio approach using chiral effective field theory interactions to compute light dark matter mediator production rates at electron fixed-target experiments, covering both elastic and quasi-elastic scattering for three nuclei (²⁰Ne, ³⁴Si, ⁵⁶Fe). Compared to a standard phenomenological parameterization, the quasi-elastic treatment increases signal yields by up to two orders of magnitude while agreeing for lighter mediators.
AI.motivation: Accelerator-based intensity frontier experiments probing light dark matter require precise modeling of the target nucleus for reliable signal predictions, motivating the need for more accurate nuclear many-body calculations beyond phenomenological approximations.
AI.method: The authors apply an ab initio many-body method with chiral effective field theory interactions to compute signal cross sections for light dark matter mediator production. They incorporate ab initio nuclear elastic form factors and spectral functions into a Monte Carlo event generator, considering both elastic and quasi-elastic scattering channels for three representative nuclei at varying electron beam energies.
AI.result: The ab initio-based quasi-elastic treatment yields signal yields up to two orders of magnitude larger than a commonly used phenomenological parameterization, while results for lighter mediators show agreement between the two approaches.
AI.conclusion: Accurate ab initio nuclear modeling significantly impacts dark matter signal rate predictions at fixed-target experiments, particularly in the quasi-elastic regime, highlighting the importance of nuclear structure input for intensity frontier searches.

title: Vortex-Antivortex Annihilation from BPS Equations
summary: In this work, we introduce a vortex-impurity model that admits BPS configurations containing both vortices and antivortices and allows vortex-antivortex annihilation to be described within the moduli-space approximation. For a suitable class of impurities, the BPS equations can be mapped through a coordinate transformation onto those of the impurity-free Abelian-Higgs model. In particular, we identify nonlocalized impurities that act as mirrors, generating a vortex-antivortex pair symmetrically placed with respect to the impurity. We derive the corresponding moduli-space metric and show that, within the geodesic approximation, the pair approaches the annihilation configuration asymptotically. We further extend the construction to chains and two-dimensional arrays of alternating vortices and antivortices. Finally, we introduce radial bump impurities that produce stretched and compressed vortices with nontrivial internal magnetic structures.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a vortex-impurity model supporting BPS configurations with both vortices and antivortices, enabling vortex-antivortex annihilation within the moduli-space approximation. Nonlocalized mirror impurities generate symmetrically placed vortex-antivortex pairs, and the derived moduli-space metric shows asymptotically approaching annihilation via geodesic approximation. The construction extends to chains and 2D arrays, and radial bump impurities produce stretched/compressed vortices with nontrivial internal magnetic structure.
AI.motivation: To develop a BPS vortex-impurity model that can accommodate both vortices and antivortices simultaneously, allowing the description of vortex-antivortex annihilation dynamics within a moduli-space framework—a capability not present in standard vortex models.
AI.method: The BPS equations are mapped via a coordinate transformation to those of the impurity-free Abelian-Higgs model for a suitable class of impurities. Nonlocalized mirror impurities generate symmetric vortex-antivortex pairs; the moduli-space metric is derived; the construction is generalized to chains and 2D arrays; radial bump impurities are introduced for stretched/compressed vortices.
AI.result: The model admits BPS vortex-antivortex configurations, mirror impurities produce symmetric pairs that approach annihilation asymptotically under geodesic motion, and the framework extends to alternating chains and two-dimensional arrays. Radial bump impurities yield vortices with deformed shapes and nontrivial internal magnetic field structures.
AI.conclusion: The vortex-impurity model provides a novel BPS framework where vortex-antivortex annihilation is tractable within moduli-space approximation, with rich generalizations to arrays and deformable vortex configurations.

title: Getting Warmer: IceCube Nears Freeze Out
comment: 7 pages, 2 figures. End Matter (5 pages, 6 figures)
summary: IceCube has recently detected a diffuse population of high-energy neutrinos arising from the Milky Way. We use this high-significance detection to place new limits on dark matter (DM) annihilation to neutrinos with two complementary approaches. The first method uses the background-subtracted Galactic longitude distribution of shower events to place a conservative bound on the DM annihilation cross section that does not rely on any assumed Galactic cosmic ray emission model; the resulting limits on the velocity-averaged annihilation cross section improve upon existing bounds by factors of a few. The second method uses the template-dependent neutrino energy spectra from the Inner Galaxy, inferred under different Galactic cosmic ray emission models. This complementary approach shows that the inferred Galactic neutrino intensities are already sensitive to DM contributions near the thermal-relic benchmark for a range of TeV-scale DM masses, though this comparison is more model-dependent. Our results demonstrate that measurements of diffuse Galactic neutrino emission can be used as a powerful probe of DM annihilation into neutrinos. Future observations with IceCube-Gen2 and KM3NeT will substantially extend this sensitivity, potentially allowing a decisive test of the thermal freeze-out mechanism with Galactic neutrino observations.

AI.tldr: Using IceCube's recent high-significance detection of diffuse high-energy neutrinos from the Milky Way, the authors place new limits on dark matter annihilation into neutrinos via two complementary methods: a model-independent bound from the Galactic longitude distribution of shower events (improving existing cross-section limits by factors of a few), and a template-dependent analysis of neutrino energy spectra from the Inner Galaxy using different cosmic ray emission models (already sensitive to DM contributions near the thermal-relic benchmark for TeV-scale masses). Future detectors like IceCube-Gen2 and KM3NeT could decisively test the thermal freeze-out mechanism.
AI.motivation: To leverage IceCube's first high-significance detection of diffuse Galactic neutrino emission as a new probe for constraining dark matter annihilation into neutrino final states, complementing existing indirect detection searches.
AI.method: Two complementary approaches are used: (1) a conservative, model-independent bound using the background-subtracted Galactic longitude distribution of shower events, avoiding assumptions about the Galactic cosmic ray emission model; (2) a template-dependent analysis of neutrino energy spectra from the Inner Galaxy inferred under different Galactic cosmic ray emission models, comparing them to DM annihilation predictions.
AI.result: The first approach yields limits on the velocity-averaged DM annihilation cross section that improve upon existing bounds by a factor of a few. The second approach finds that inferred Galactic neutrino intensities are already sensitive to DM contributions near the thermal-relic benchmark for TeV-scale DM masses, though with greater model dependence.
AI.conclusion: Diffuse Galactic neutrino emission measurements serve as a powerful probe of DM annihilation into neutrinos. Future observations with IceCube-Gen2 and KM3NeT could substantially extend sensitivity and potentially enable a decisive test of the thermal freeze-out mechanism for dark matter.

title: The Capacity of Entanglement and Holographic Entropies at Finite Resources
summary:
The Ryu-Takayanagi formula equates the area of a minimal surface with the von Neumann entropy of a boundary subregion, and leaves two things about that identification open.
  The first is how sharply a geometry fixes an entropy. Fannes-Audenaert answers with a Hilbert-space dimension, which diverges as the cutoff is removed however close the two states are. We replace it with the capacity of entanglement, the variance of the modular energy, whose square root grows like the square root of the entangling area where the dimensional factor grows like the regulated volume. The bound is dimension-free and saturated, and it makes the ambiguity of the entropy subextensive for any perturbation whose capacity is small compared with $S_{vN}^2$ times the trace norm.
  The second is what the area means for a single state, since compression and dilution rates are defined only for many copies while a geometry describes one. When a single replica saddle dominates near $α= 1$, every smooth Rényi entropy at fixed $α> 1$ agrees with $S_{vN}$ to $\textit{O}(\sqrt{S_{vN}})$, as do the smooth min- and max-entropies. The minimal surface therefore fixes every one-shot entropy of the state at once, with large central charge playing the role of large copy number in the asymptotic equipartition property.
  As a consequence we bound how far outside the holographic entropy cone a holographic state can appear to fall, leaving estimation and certification open.

AI.tldr: This paper addresses two open questions about the Ryu-Takayanagi (RT) formula. First, it replaces the dimension-dependent Fannes-Audenaert bound on entropy ambiguity with a dimension-free bound based on the capacity of entanglement, showing entropy ambiguity is subextensive when capacity is small. Second, it shows that when a single replica saddle dominates near α=1, all smooth Rényi entropies agree with S_vN to O(√S_vN), establishing that the minimal surface fixes all one-shot entropies simultaneously, with large central charge playing the role of large copy number.
AI.motivation: The RT formula identifies minimal surface area with von Neumann entropy, but leaves open two fundamental questions: (1) how precisely a geometry determines an entropy (the Fannes-Audenaert bound depends on Hilbert space dimension, diverging as the cutoff is removed), and (2) what the area means for a single holographic state, since standard compression/dilution rates are defined only for many copies while a geometry describes a single state.
AI.method: The paper derives a dimension-free uncertainty bound for the entropy using the capacity of entanglement (variance of modular energy), whose growth is subextensive compared to the Fannes-Audenaert dimensional factor. For the one-shot aspect, it analyzes smooth Rényi entropies near α=1 when a single replica saddle dominates, proving they all agree with S_vN to O(√S_vN), analogous to the asymptotic equipartition property with large central charge replacing copy number.
AI.result: The capacity-of-entanglement bound is dimension-free, saturated, and shows entropy ambiguity is subextensive for perturbations with small capacity compared to S_vN² times trace norm. When a single replica saddle dominates near α=1, every smooth Rényi entropy at fixed α>1 agrees with S_vN to O(√S_vN), as do the smooth min- and max-entropies. The minimal surface consequently fixes all one-shot entropies simultaneously.
AI.conclusion: The minimal surface determines not just the von Neumann entropy but all one-shot entropies of a holographic state, with large central charge enabling the single-state analogs of asymptotic equipartition. The results also bound how far a holographic state can appear to violate the holographic entropy cone, leaving estimation and certification as open problems.

title: Enhancement of nonlinear pair production in a flying-focus pulse
summary: A photon can decay into an electron-positron pair in the presence of an intense laser pulse by a process known as nonlinear Breit-Wheeler pair production (NBWPP). For a sufficiently intense pulse, the probability of NBWPP for a high-energy gamma photon scales more favorably with the interaction time than with the field intensity. In contrast to typical stationary-focus Gaussian (SFG) laser pulses, a flying-focus (FF) pulse features a focal point that moves at a programmable velocity. Here, we show that a FF pulse counterpropagating with a high-energy photon beam while its focus copropagates with the beam at the speed of light enhances the NBWPP yield relative to an equal-energy SFG pulse. Numerical simulations show that a Joule-class tightly-focused FF pulse allows for an enhancement of the pair-production yield by 12\%, 29\% and 76\% for a photon of 10, 20 and 50 GeV energy, respectively. Thus, in this regime, FF pulses are more efficient at producing electron-positron pairs than conventional SFG pulses.

AI.tldr: The paper shows that flying-focus (FF) laser pulses, whose focal point moves at a programmable velocity, can enhance nonlinear Breit-Wheeler pair production (NBWPP) yield compared to standard stationary-focus Gaussian (SFG) pulses when the focus copropagates with a counterpropagating high-energy photon beam at the speed of light. Simulations indicate yield enhancements of 12%, 29%, and 76% for photon energies of 10, 20, and 50 GeV, respectively, using a Joule-class tightly-focused FF pulse.
AI.motivation: NBWPP probability scales more favorably with interaction time than field intensity for sufficiently intense pulses. Since conventional SFG pulses have a fixed focal geometry, they limit the interaction time between the laser and high-energy photons. A FF pulse whose focus moves at a controllable velocity offers a way to extend the effective interaction time, potentially improving pair-production efficiency.
AI.method: The authors consider a flying-focus pulse counterpropagating with a high-energy photon beam, where the FF focal point copropagates with the photon beam at the speed of light. They compare the NBWPP yield of this configuration against an equal-energy SFG pulse using numerical simulations, scanning photon energies of 10, 20, and 50 GeV with a Joule-class tightly-focused pulse.
AI.result: Numerical simulations show that the FF pulse enhances the pair-production yield relative to an equal-energy SFG pulse by 12% at 10 GeV, 29% at 20 GeV, and 76% at 50 GeV photon energy.
AI.conclusion: In the regime studied, flying-focus pulses are more efficient at producing electron-positron pairs than conventional stationary-focus Gaussian pulses, demonstrating that the programmable focal motion of FF pulses offers a practical advantage for nonlinear Breit-Wheeler pair production.

title: Scalar QED effective action in dS: implications for primordial magnetogenesis and the running of coupling constants
summary: Particles creation and vacuum polarization under the influence of both an electromagnetic field and a de~Sitter (dS) spacetime nonperturbatively probes quantum electrodynamics (QED) and quantum gravitational effects. By applying the gamma-function regularization to the in-out formulation, we find the exact one-loop effective action in the proper-time integral representation for a charged scalar field in a uniform electric field and a parallel magnetic field in a dS spacetime. It reduces to the one-loop scalar QED Weisskopf-Schwinger effective action in the limit of Minkowski spacetime and the one-loop effective action in the pure dS spacetime. After carefully considering the different limiting cases, a striking result concerns the effective strengths of the coupling constants in the pure strong electric field limit. Our study provides further evidence for evolution of Newton's gravitational constant under the influence of the external fields. Remarkably, the analysis of the effective potential shows that the leading order contributions to the vacuum polarization amplitude, depending on the nonminimal coupling threshold, give a nonzero vacuum expectation value of the magnetic field. This mechanism generates a large magnetic field in the early dS stage of the expansion that may imply primordial magnetogenesis.

AI.tldr: The paper computes the exact one-loop effective action for a charged scalar field in dS spacetime under uniform electric and parallel magnetic fields using gamma-function regularization in the in-out formalism. It reveals coupling constant renormalization in the strong-field limit and shows that vacuum polarization can generate a non-zero magnetic field expectation value, potentially explaining primordial magnetogenesis in the early dS universe.
AI.motivation: To nonperturbatively probe combined QED and quantum gravitational effects by studying particle creation and vacuum polarization in the presence of both electromagnetic fields and dS spacetime curvature.
AI.method: Uses the in-out formulation with gamma-function regularization to derive the exact one-loop effective action in proper-time integral representation for a charged scalar field subject to uniform electric and parallel magnetic fields in dS spacetime. The result is checked against known limits (Minkowski spacetime and pure dS limits).
AI.result: The effective action reduces correctly to the Weisskopf-Schwinger effective action in the Minkowski limit and the pure dS effective action. In the strong electric field limit, the effective coupling constants (including Newton's gravitational constant) are altered. The effective potential analysis shows leading-order vacuum polarization contributions yield a non-zero vacuum expectation value for the magnetic field when the nonminimal coupling threshold is considered.
AI.conclusion: The findings provide evidence for the evolution of Newton's gravitational constant under external fields and suggest a mechanism for generating large magnetic fields during the early dS stage of cosmic expansion, potentially accounting for primordial magnetogenesis.

title: Direct and Indirect searches for DM-electron interactions in sub-GeV DM models
summary: We analyze the complementarity between direct detection (DD) and indirect detection (ID) searches of sub-GeV dark matter (DM) in the context of two realistic models: the vector-portal (dark photon) and scalar-portal (higgs-portal) models. For DD we focus on the latest constraints on the DM-electron scattering from the present DAMIC-M experiment as well as its future projection. For ID we consider several existing X-rays/gamma-rays and cosmic-ray ($e^\pm$) observations as well as the upcoming MeV telescope COSI to obtain the corresponding bounds and projections on the DM annihilation rate, which are then translated in terms of the DM-electron scattering cross-section and compared with the DD bounds/projections. We properly take into account astrophysical and galactic propagation uncertainties. We find that the complementarity between DAMIC-M and ID works best for the vector-portal model, especially for the case where the vector mediator is heavier than the DM particle: in this case, the present DAMIC-M bound becomes comparable to (or better than, for some astrophysical configurations) the combined ID limit for $3\,{\rm MeV} \lesssim m_{\rm DM} \lesssim 20\,{\rm MeV}$. For other cases and mass ranges, the ID is in general more constraining and can also, for some mass ranges, constrain the parameter space below the neutrino floor, which is inaccessible to DD experiments.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes the complementarity between direct detection (DAMIC-M) and indirect detection (X-rays/gamma-rays/cosmic-rays) searches for sub-GeV dark matter in two realistic models (vector-portal and scalar-portal), finding that complementarity works best for the vector-portal model with a heavier mediator, where DD bounds become comparable to ID limits for DM masses between 3-20 MeV, while ID generally provides stronger constraints and can probe below the neutrino floor.
AI.motivation: To understand how direct and indirect detection searches complement each other for sub-GeV dark matter, a mass range where traditional detection methods face challenges, and to determine which model scenarios benefit most from combined searches.
AI.method: The authors compare DM-electron scattering bounds from DAMIC-M (present and projected) against indirect detection constraints from X-rays, gamma-rays, and cosmic-ray e± observations (including the upcoming COSI telescope). They translate indirect detection limits on annihilation rates into DM-electron scattering cross-sections, properly accounting for astrophysical and galactic propagation uncertainties.
AI.result: The complementarity between DAMIC-M and indirect detection works best for the vector-portal model with a mediator heavier than the DM particle, where DAMIC-M bounds become comparable or better than combined ID limits for 3-20 MeV DM masses. In other scenarios, indirect detection is generally more constraining and can probe parameter space below the neutrino floor inaccessible to direct detection.
AI.conclusion: The relative power of direct vs. indirect detection for sub-GeV DM depends strongly on the model (vector vs. scalar portal), the mass hierarchy between mediator and DM, and the astrophysical assumptions. Indirect detection remains the dominant probe in most cases for sub-GeV DM, but direct detection can be competitive in specific vector-portal scenarios.

title: Quantum Chaos and Spread of States in Krylov Subspace: A Topical Review
comment: 39 pages, 29 figures, 1 Mathematica notebook; Invited review for the special issue "Krylov Complexity Across Scales: From Quantum Many-Body Systems to Black Holes" for the Journal of Physics A: Mathematical and Theoretical
summary: Krylov state complexity, or spread complexity, has emerged as a sharp and versatile diagnostic of quantum chaos, information spreading, and many-body dynamics. Built from the Lanczos algorithm and grounded in the optimal-basis theorem, Krylov complexity thereby provides a robust spectroscopic window into quantum dynamics. A central theme is the characteristic overshoot observed in chaotic systems: a complexity peak in which chaotic evolution drives the state deeper into the Krylov chain than in integrable systems before relaxing to equilibrium. This behavior, tied to random-matrix universality classes of spectral statistics, is illustrated across a broad range of models, including quantum billiards, quantum spin chains, and variants of the SYK model. We also discuss proposed holographic descriptions of Krylov complexity in Einstein gravity, and conclude by outlining future directions and open problems, including time-dependent systems and quantum-field-theoretic formulations. A Mathematica notebook is provided for numerical exploration of Krylov complexity and spectral statistics across models.

AI.tldr: This paper provides a comprehensive review of Krylov state complexity (spread complexity) as a diagnostic of quantum chaos, information spreading, and many-body dynamics. It covers the theoretical foundations (Lanczos algorithm, optimal-basis theorem), the characteristic overshoot behavior in chaotic systems tied to random-matrix universality classes, applications across quantum billiards, spin chains, and SYK variants, proposed holographic descriptions in Einstein gravity, and future directions including time-dependent systems and QFT formulations. A Mathematica notebook is included for numerical exploration.
AI.motivation: To establish Krylov/spread complexity as a sharp and versatile diagnostic of quantum chaos and information spreading, grounded in the Lanczos algorithm and optimal-basis theorem, and to provide a unified framework for understanding complexity growth across diverse quantum systems.
AI.method: The paper employs the Krylov/Lanczos construction to define a complexity measure on the Krylov basis, identifying characteristic overshoot phenomena in chaotic systems linked to random-matrix universality classes. It illustrates these features across multiple model systems (quantum billiards, spin chains, SYK variants) and discusses holographic dual descriptions in Einstein gravity, complemented by a computational Mathematica notebook.
AI.result: Chaotic systems exhibit a characteristic complexity overshoot—a peak driving the state deeper into the Krylov chain than integrable systems—before relaxing to equilibrium. This behavior is tied to random-matrix universality classes of spectral statistics and is demonstrated across quantum billiards, spin chains, and SYK variants.
AI.conclusion: Krylov complexity provides a robust spectroscopic window into quantum dynamics. The paper outlines future directions including time-dependent systems, quantum-field-theoretic formulations, and open problems, while making numerical tools publicly available.

title: Atomic structure calculations for constraining new electron-electron forces
summary: We present a general approach for calculating new electron-electron interactions with atomic structure theory, include dominant many-body effects, and extract bounds for parity-odd cases. The procedure is valid for any mediator mass and improves previous calculations by including many-body corrections to the new interaction through the time-dependent Hartree-Fock method. Bounds on coupling strengths are then extracted for scalar-pseudoscalar and vector-axial vector interactions by comparison with experimental atomic electric dipole moments and parity non-conserving (PNC) transitions respectively. In the latter case, our calculations rule out any coupling-mass ratio |g^e_V g^e_A|/m_X^2 greater than 10^-11 MeV^-2 above m_X ~ 10 MeV, covering a previously unconstrained mass region. We also report an updated calculation of the regular (Standard Model) electron-electron Z^0 exchange contribution to the 6s-7s PNC transition amplitude E_PNC in cesium.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a general method for computing new electron-electron interactions using atomic structure theory, incorporating many-body effects via the time-dependent Hartree-Fock method, and extracting bounds on coupling strengths for scalar-pseudoscalar and vector-axial vector interactions using atomic EDM and parity non-conserving measurements.
AI.motivation: Previous calculations of new electron-electron interactions lacked many-body corrections and were limited in mass range. The authors aim to provide a general, improved framework valid for any mediator mass and to probe previously unconstrained parameter space.
AI.method: The approach uses atomic structure theory with the time-dependent Hartree-Fock method to include dominant many-body corrections to new electron-electron interactions. Bounds are extracted by comparing with experimental atomic electric dipole moments (for scalar-pseudoscalar) and parity non-conserving transitions (for vector-axial vector). An updated calculation of the Standard Model Z^0 exchange contribution to the 6s-7s PNC transition amplitude in cesium is also reported.
AI.result: For vector-axial vector interactions, the calculations rule out coupling-mass ratios |g^e_V g^e_A|/m_X^2 greater than 10^-11 MeV^-2 for mediator masses above ~10 MeV, covering a previously unconstrained mass region. The method is valid for any mediator mass.
AI.conclusion: The general framework improves prior bounds through many-body corrections and extends sensitivity to new mass regions, providing tighter constraints on new electron-electron interactions and an updated Standard Model PNC amplitude in cesium.

title: The Hydrotope in the Water-Wave Action
summary: The Hydrotope gives a geometric representation of tree-level water-wave amplitudes with two negative spatial momenta as the volume of a hyperplane slice of a box. We trace the origin of this geometry directly to the water-wave action. Writing the $n$-point contact interaction as $\mathcal{V}_n=\sum_{i<j}w_iw_jh_{ij}^{(n)}$, we show that when the two marked momenta have the same sign and every spectator has the opposite sign, the corresponding coefficient is $h_{ij}^{(n)}=2H_n$, where $H_n/(n{-}3)!$ is the Hydrotope volume. More generally, every fixed-pair coefficient admits a denominator-free ordered-flag representation as an oriented sum of $(n{-}3)$-dimensional box volumes. We then sum all two-minus trees by cutting each at the unique vertex joining its two minus branches. The coefficients multiplying minus-minus, minus-plus, and plus-plus frequency bilinears reduce, respectively, to $(2^{n{-}1}{-}2)H_n$, $0$, and $2H_n$, and immediately reproduce the known amplitude $2^{n{-}1}w_1w_2H_n$. Thus, the Hydrotope-and a broader class of related box-slice geometries-is already encoded locally in the water-wave action. This points to further hidden simplicity and geometric structure in general water-wave amplitudes.

AI.tldr: The paper traces the geometric origin of the "Hydrotope" (a hyperplane-sliced box volume representing tree-level water-wave amplitudes with two negative spatial momenta) directly to the water-wave action, showing that the relevant Feynman coefficients are Hydrotope volumes and that summing two-minus trees reduces to known amplitudes, revealing hidden geometric simplicity in water-wave amplitudes.
AI.motivation: To explain why tree-level water-wave amplitudes admit a purely geometric (Hydrotope) representation by tracing its origin to the underlying water-wave action, and to show this geometry is not an emergent coincidence but is locally encoded in the action itself.
AI.method: The paper writes the n-point contact interaction as V_n = sum_{i<j} w_i w_j h_{ij}^{(n)} and proves that when the two marked momenta have the same sign with all spectators of the opposite sign, the coefficient satisfies h_{ij}^{(n)} = 2H_n (where H_n/(n-3)! is the Hydrotope volume). It further establishes that every fixed-pair coefficient admits a denominator-free ordered-flag representation as an oriented sum of (n-3)-dimensional box volumes. The summation over all two-minus trees is performed by cutting each tree at the unique vertex joining its two minus branches, yielding coefficients for minus-minus, minus-plus, and plus-plus frequency bilinears.
AI.result: The reduced coefficients multiplying minus-minus, minus-plus, and plus-plus frequency bilinears are respectively (2^{n-1}-2)H_n, 0, and 2H_n, which reproduce the known amplitude 2^{n-1} w_1 w_2 H_n exactly.
AI.conclusion: The Hydrotope geometry and a broader class of box-slice geometries are already encoded locally in the water-wave action, indicating further hidden simplicity and geometric structure in general water-wave amplitudes.

title: Fermi gas of domain-wall Skyrmions in QCD in a strong magnetic field
summary: Fermionic domain-wall Skyrmions arise in the chiral soliton lattice of two flavor chiral perturbation theory in a magnetic field as the ground state and are associated with baryons of the underlying theory of quantum chromodynamics. We analyze the electromagnetic screening characteristics of domain-wall Skyrmions that give insight into baryon density on the magnetic field and chemical potential phase diagram. At zero temperature, using the moduli effective theory, it is found Skyrmion density is saturated up to the Fermi momenta on the disk of the chiral soliton lattice orthogonal to the magnetic field. We further study chiral perturbation theory coupled to quantum electrodynamics leading to finite temperature screening, wherein a static fermionic domain-wall Skyrmion screening is predicted through a combined Debye mass/length.

AI.tldr: The paper analyzes electromagnetic screening of fermionic domain-wall Skyrmions in the chiral soliton lattice of two-flavor chiral perturbation theory in a magnetic field. At zero temperature, Skyrmion density saturates up to the Fermi momenta on the disk orthogonal to the magnetic field via the moduli effective theory. At finite temperature, coupling chiral perturbation theory to QED yields a combined Debye mass/length screening prediction for static fermionic domain-wall Skyrmions.
AI.motivation: To understand the electromagnetic screening properties of domain-wall Skyrmions, which are associated with baryons in QCD, and to gain insight into baryon density across the magnetic field and chemical potential phase diagram.
AI.method: The study uses the moduli effective theory at zero temperature to analyze Skyrmion density saturation up to Fermi momenta on the disk of the chiral soliton lattice perpendicular to the magnetic field. It also couples chiral perturbation theory to quantum electrodynamics to study finite-temperature screening effects, deriving a combined Debye mass/length for static fermionic domain-wall Skyrmion screening.
AI.result: At zero temperature, the Skyrmion density is saturated up to the Fermi momenta on the disk of the chiral soliton lattice orthogonal to the magnetic field. At finite temperature, a static fermionic domain-wall Skyrmion screening is predicted through a combined Debye mass/length.
AI.conclusion: Domain-wall Skyrmions exhibit characteristic electromagnetic screening behavior that reveals their baryonic nature, with density saturation at zero temperature and Debye-type screening at finite temperature when coupled to QED.

title: Testing holographic computation of entanglement pseudo-entropy in dS\textsubscript{3}/ICFT\textsubscript{2}
summary: We establish a bottom-up model for studying the `would-be' de-Sitter/interface CFT (dS/ICFT) correspondence on the gravity side, using the Coleman-De Luccia instanton. After absorbing the region where the inflaton changes dramatically by a brane, the spacetime consists of two de Sitter spacetimes with different radii joined by a brane, which is expected to be dual to an interface CFT provided that the dS/CFT conjecture is correct. Our goal is to analyze existing prescriptions for the holographic computation of pseudo-entropy, i.e. the extremal surface in such a spacetime and argue that some of them would cause parodox with the results expected the universal properties of interface CFT and compare our results with that of Anti de Sitter/interface CFT correspondence (AdS/ICFT) after analytic continuation. We also read off the $g$-function from the entanglement entropy associated with a subregion perpendicular to the interface.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs a bottom-up gravity model for the dS/ICFT correspondence using the Coleman-De Luccia instanton as the background, studying holographic pseudo-entropy prescriptions and comparing with AdS/ICFT via analytic continuation.
AI.motivation: To investigate the dS/ICFT correspondence and identify potential paradoxes in existing holographic pseudo-entropy prescriptions, while establishing connections to the better-understood AdS/ICFT framework.
AI.method: The authors model the spacetime as two de Sitter spacetimes with different radii joined by a brane (after absorbing the inflaton transition region into the brane). They analyze extremal surface prescriptions for pseudo-entropy holographically and compare with AdS/ICFT results via analytic continuation. They also compute the g-function from entanglement entropy of a region perpendicular to the interface.
AI.result: The analysis shows that some existing holographic prescriptions for pseudo-entropy lead to paradoxes inconsistent with the universal properties expected of interface CFTs. The comparison with AdS/ICFT after analytic continuation clarifies discrepancies, and a g-function is extracted from the subregion entanglement entropy.
AI.conclusion: Certain pseudo-entropy prescriptions in dS/ICFT are inconsistent with interface CFT universal properties, and the correct approach is constrained by comparison with AdS/ICFT; the g-function offers a concrete universal quantity to test the correspondence.

title: Post-sphaleron conversion between baryon and lepton numbers
summary: The conversion between baryon and lepton numbers has a significant impact on the mechanisms for dynamically generating the matter-antimatter asymmetry in the present universe. Under the traditional wisdom, such conversion originates from the so-called electroweak sphaleron processes. In this work we find that in association with a proper scalar and the other TeV new physics, the baryon-lepton conversion can still keep efficient after the electroweak sphalerons are no longer active. Moreover this scenario can provide a solution to the puzzle of neutron lifetime and predict some decay modes of multi-nucleons to multi-leptons.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a new mechanism for baryon-lepton number conversion that remains efficient even after electroweak sphaleron processes cease, potentially solving the neutron lifetime puzzle and predicting multi-nucleon to multi-lepton decays.
AI.motivation: The conversion between baryon and lepton numbers is crucial for understanding the dynamical generation of matter-antimatter asymmetry. Traditionally, this is attributed to electroweak sphaleron processes, but exploring alternative mechanisms beyond this framework is important.
AI.method: The authors introduce a new physics scenario involving a proper scalar field and additional TeV-scale new physics that allows baryon-lepton conversion to remain efficient after sphalerons are no longer active.
AI.result: The scenario provides a solution to the neutron lifetime puzzle and predicts observable decay modes of multi-nucleons to multi-leptons.
AI.conclusion: Baryon-lepton conversion need not rely solely on sphaleron processes; alternative TeV-scale mechanisms with scalar fields can sustain such conversions, with testable phenomenological consequences.

title: Wess-Zumino gauge for analytic prepotentials of off-shell $\mathcal{N}=2$ supergravity: bosonic sector
summary: We present a comprehensive study of the Wess-Zumino gauge for the analytic prepotentials of the off-shell $\mathcal{N}=2$ Weyl and $\mathcal{N}=2$ Einstein supergravities (the version with a non-linear tensor compensator). The field redefinitions, the full transformation laws, and the gauge superparameters that preserve the Wess-Zumino gauge are derived. As a concrete application of the obtained results, we examine the component structure of the free hypermultiplet action coupled to $\mathcal{N}=2$ supergravity. In this work, we restrict our analysis strictly to the bosonic sector.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a comprehensive study of the Wess-Zumino gauge for off-shell N=2 Weyl and Einstein supergravities, deriving field redefinitions, transformation laws, and gauge superparameters that preserve this gauge. It applies these results to examine the bosonic component structure of a free hypermultiplet action coupled to N=2 supergravity.
AI.motivation: The authors aim to provide a systematic framework for working in the Wess-Zumino gauge for analytic prepotentials in N=2 supergravity theories, which is essential for practical component-level calculations. Understanding this gauge enables concrete applications such as coupling matter actions to supergravity.
AI.method: The study systematically derives the Wess-Zumino gauge conditions for the analytic prepotentials in off-shell N=2 Weyl and Einstein supergravities (the latter using a non-linear tensor compensator). The authors derive the field redefinitions, full transformation laws, and identify gauge superparameters that preserve the Wess-Zumino gauge. They then apply these results to analyze the bosonic component structure of the free hypermultiplet action coupled to N=2 supergravity.
AI.result: The paper successfully derives the complete set of field redefinitions, transformation laws, and gauge-fixing superparameters for the Wess-Zumino gauge in N=2 Weyl and Einstein supergravities. As a concrete application, the bosonic sector of the free hypermultiplet action coupled to N=2 supergravity is examined in component form.
AI.conclusion: The work provides a complete and systematic treatment of the Wess-Zumino gauge for on-shell prepotentials in N=2 supergravities, with results applicable to component-level analyses. The analysis is deliberately restricted to the bosonic sector, leaving fermionic contributions for future work.

title: From Thermal History to Multi-Messenger Signatures in $\mathbb{Z}_3$ Symmetric Dark Sector
summary: We investigate a $\mathbb{Z}_3$-symmetric extension of the Standard Model consisting of a right-handed neutrino ($N_R$), a dark fermion ($χ$) that dominates the relic density and a dark complex scalar ($S$) that facilitates a strong first-order electroweak phase transition (SFOEWPT). The observed relic abundance, is achieved through the combined effects of annihilation, semi-annihilation, and dark-sector conversion processes over a broad region of parameter space consistent with a SFOEWPT. We further investigate the resulting multi-messenger signatures, including loop-induced direct detection, indirect detection through gamma-ray observations, and gravitational wave signals, with the latter lying within the projected sensitivities of future space-based detectors such as LISA, BBO, and DECIGO.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a Z3-symmetric extension of the Standard Model with a right-handed neutrino, a dark fermion serving as dark matter, and a complex scalar facilitating a strong first-order electroweak phase transition, while exploring relic density, direct/indirect detection signatures, and gravitational wave signals within future detector sensitivities.
AI.motivation: To extend the Standard Model to simultaneously address dark matter, the electroweak phase transition (for baryogenesis), and generate multi-messenger signatures that can be tested by future experiments.
AI.method: Constructs a Z3-symmetric model with three new fields (N_R, χ, S), computes the dark matter relic abundance through annihilation, semi-annihilation, and dark-sector conversion processes, and analyzes loop-induced direct detection, gamma-ray indirect detection, and stochastic gravitational wave signals from the strong first-order electroweak phase transition.
AI.result: The observed relic abundance can be achieved over a broad parameter space consistent with a strong first-order electroweak phase transition. The resulting gravitational wave signals fall within the projected sensitivities of LISA, BBO, and DECIGO, providing testable predictions.
AI.conclusion: The Z3-symmetric extension provides a viable framework connecting dark matter, electroweak baryogenesis, and multi-messenger observables including gravitational waves detectable by future space-based observatories.

title: Quantum Selection of Classical Histories
summary: Can a finite quantum episode populate a classical future that the same prepared state never reaches deterministically? We show that it can, using inflation as a cosmological laboratory. In our supergravity realization, two classical continuations already exist, but the prepared state reaches only one without noise. A stable entropy direction temporarily becomes light without a tachyonic instability, allowing mode-derived phase-space fluctuations to access the competing continuation. Finite-horizon first passage assigns it a \(0.33\)--\(0.40\) conditional weight across three nearby CMB-normalized realizations, while suppressing the stochastic source restores its exact deterministic zero. The entropy sector then becomes heavy again, and the selected histories continue classically. A finite quantum episode can thus leave a lasting redistribution among classical futures.

AI.tldr: The paper demonstrates that a finite quantum episode can redistribute probabilities among classical futures in an inflationary cosmological context. Using supergravity, two classical continuations exist, but the prepared state reaches only one deterministically. A stable entropy direction temporarily becomes light (without tachyonic instability), allowing mode-derived phase-space fluctuations to access the competing continuation, which receives a 0.33–0.40 conditional weight across three CMB-normalized realizations.

title: $μ$DM: a new mechanism for the baryon-dark matter coincidence
summary: For a relativistically decoupled thermal relic, the dark-matter energy-to-entropy ratio scales as $ρ_{\rm DM}/s\sim 10^{-3}m_{\rm DM}$. This is the familiar hot-dark-matter abundance relation. Immediately after weak-sphaleron freeze-out, the baryon asymmetry can be parametrized as $ρ_{\rm baryon}/s\sim 10^{-4}|μ_B|$. Here $μ_B$ is the baryon-number chemical potential. We propose a new class of models, called chemical-potential-matched dark matter ($μ$DM), in which $|μ_B|\sim m_{\rm DM}$, thereby providing a new route to the baryon-dark matter coincidence. As a concrete example of $μ$DM, we consider an Affleck-Dine field whose excitations constitute dark matter. We also briefly discuss spontaneous electroweak baryogenesis associated with axion-like-particle walls. In the absence of entropy dilution, this coincidence mechanism generically points to dark matter in the eV-keV mass range. Its momentum distribution can nevertheless be cold if thermal production is dominated by Bose-enhanced stimulated emission. Alternatively, entropy dilution after both the dark-matter and baryon yields are fixed allows masses up to the MeV scale.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a new class of dark matter models called "chemical-potential-matched dark matter" (μDM), where the baryon-number chemical potential is matched to the dark matter mass scale, providing a novel solution to the baryon-dark matter coincidence problem. A concrete example using an Affleck-Dine field is given, with dark matter masses typically in the eV-keV range (or up to MeV with entropy dilution).

Existing mechanisms often require fine-tuning or unrelated parameters. The authors seek a new physical connection between the dark matter mass and the baryon asymmetry generation process that naturally yields comparable energy densities.
