By requiring |μ_B| ~ m_DM, the hot-dark-matter abundance relation ρ_DM/s ~ 10^-3 m_DM naturally yields the correct baryon-to-dark-matter ratio. A concrete realization is proposed via an Affleck-Dine field whose excitations form dark matter. The authors also discuss spontaneous electroweak baryogenesis with axion-like-particle walls as an alternative implementation, and analyze the resulting dark matter mass range and momentum distribution (including the possibility of cold dark matter via Bose-enhanced stimulated emission, or entropy dilution to allow MeV-scale masses).
AI.result: The paper establishes that in the μDM framework, without entropy dilution, dark matter masses are generically in the eV-keV range. However, the dark matter can still be cold if thermal production is dominated by Bose-enhanced stimulated emission. Alternatively, entropy dilution after both yields are fixed allows dark matter masses up to around the MeV scale.
AI.conclusion: The chemical-potential-matched dark matter mechanism provides a new, natural route to explaining the baryon-dark matter coincidence by linking the baryon chemical potential to the dark matter mass. The framework yields testable predictions for dark matter mass scales (eV-keV, or up to MeV with entropy dilution) and opens new model-building directions, such as Affleck-Dine dark matter and electroweak baryogenesis with ALP walls.

title: Doubly-scaled planar ${\cal N} = 4$ SYM \& Carroll Holography
summary: Okuda and Penedones (OP) \cite{Okuda:2010ym} showed the existence of a double scaling limit of four point correlators in ${\cal N}=4$ Supersymmetric Yang Mills (SYM) theory in four spacetime dimensions (4$d$) dual to the flat space limit of tree-level string amplitude in $\mathbb{R}^{1,9}$ with external kinematics in $\mathbb{R}^{1,4}$. In this paper, we show that the resulting boundary correlators can be used to define a 4d Carrollian conformal field theory (CFT) on future null infinity (${\I}^{+}$). This is done by mapping the set of correlators in ${\cal N} = 4$ SYM theory (in the double scaling limit) to ${\I}^{+}$, which is the conformal boundary of all asymptotically flat spacetimes. A Carroll CFT thus emerges in the infinite 't Hooft coupling limit of ${\cal N} = 4$ SYM theory. We extend the OP analysis to higher point functions and show how the Gram conditions on flat space amplitude put constraints on the double scaling limit of SYM correlators. We then use the soft factorization theorem for dilatonic string amplitude to write a recursion relation for $\frac{1}{2}$ BPS sector of ${\cal N} = 4$ SYM theory in the double scaling limit. Finally, we show that the essential ideas underlying such a double scaling limit can be used as a tool-kit to build a class of Carrollian correlators, and hence define a Carrollian CFT, via certain integral transforms of flat space amplitudes of non-gravitational effective field theories.

This Carrollian CFT emerges in the infinite 't Hooft coupling limit. The authors extend the analysis to higher-point functions, derive a recursion relation for 1/2 BPS correlators using soft factorization theorems, and propose a general toolkit for constructing Carrollian CFTs from flat space amplitudes via integral transforms.

Building on the Okuda-Penedones double scaling limit provides a rigorous path to map SYM correlators to null infinity and thus construct a Carrollian CFT from a well-understood AdS/CFT setup.

They extend the OP analysis to higher-point functions, impose Gram conditions on flat space amplitudes to constrain the double scaling limit, use soft factorization theorems for dilatonic string amplitudes to derive recursion relations for 1/2 BPS correlators, and propose a general integral-transform toolkit to construct Carrollian correlators from flat space amplitudes of non-gravitational EFTs.

Higher-point correlators are obtained with Gram condition constraints, a recursion relation for 1/2 BPS correlators is derived, and a general framework is established for building Carrollian CFTs from flat space amplitudes through integral transforms.
AI.conclusion: The double scaling limit of N=4 SYM provides a concrete realization of Carrollian holography on I+, and the proposed toolkit offers a systematic method to construct Carrollian CFTs from flat space amplitudes, potentially connecting AdS/CFT to flat space holography more broadly.

title: Simulations and flavour-scheme studies for Higgs-boson production in association with charm quarks
comment: Contribution to the Report 5 collection of the LHC Higgs Working Group. Also available at the CERN Document Server: https://cds.cern.ch/record/2965814
summary: We present a detailed NLO+PS study of Higgs-boson production in association with charm and bottom quarks, with particular focus on the modelling of the H+c final state. We systematically compare predictions in massive and massless flavour schemes, quantify scale and flavour-scheme uncertainties, and assess the impact of interference and loop-induced contributions. Special emphasis is placed on the Higgs production via charm Yukawa fusion, for which we compare NLO+PS predictions with a NNLO+PS calculation of $c\bar{c}H$ production in the four-flavour scheme at 13.6 TeV. Based on these results, we provide the first practical recommendations for the simulation of $c\bar{c}H$ production in LHC analyses.

AI.method: Systematic comparison of NLO+PS predictions in massive (4-flavour) and massless (5-flavour) schemes for H+charm and H+bottom production, including scale and flavour-scheme uncertainty quantification, assessment of interference and loop-induced contributions, and comparison of NLO+PS predictions with a NNLO+PS calculation for ccH production in the four-flavour scheme at 13.6 TeV.

AI.conclusion: Practical simulation recommendations for ccH production in LHC analyses are established, grounded in systematic comparisons across flavour schemes and perturbative orders, addressing the modelling of the H+c final state.

title: Advances in the holographic description of hot and dense QCD matter
comment: 39 pages, 19 figures, invited review for Annals of Physics ("Quantum Phases of Strong Dynamics")
summary: We review and extend recent progress on QCD-like phases at nonzero temperature and chemical potentials within the gauge-gravity duality. We focus on the Witten-Sakai-Sugimoto model, a top-down approach based on string theory which allows for a unified treatment of mesons, baryons and quarks. Phases such as pion condensation, baryonic and quarkyonic matter are located in the phase diagram, and we discuss predictions as well as weaknesses and limitations of this holographic approach. One of the novelties included in this review is the first holographic construction of a pionic phase between BEC and BCS regimes, which however is found to be metastable. We also discuss future directions in holographic QCD, within the model used here and in a wider context.

It maps the phase diagram including pion condensation, baryonic, and quarkyonic phases, and introduces a novel (though metastable) holographic pionic phase between BEC and BCS regimes, while discussing limitations and future directions.

AI.method: The paper employs the Witten-Sakai-Sugimoto model, a top-down holographic construction from string theory, to analyze QCD-like phases at finite temperature and chemical potential. It maps out pion condensation, baryonic, and quarkyonic phases in the phase diagram and constructs the first holographic pionic phase interpolating between BEC and BCS regimes.

AI.conclusion: The holographic approach via the Witten-Sakai-Sugimoto model provides a unified top-down framework for studying QCD-like phases, with the new BEC-BCS pionic phase being a notable but metastable addition. Future directions in holographic QCD within and beyond this model are outlined.

title: Proof of the AGT Conjecture at Generic $β$
summary: We give an all-level proof of the four-point $SU(2)$ AGT correspondence with four fundamental hypermultiplets at generic $β=-ε_1/ε_2$, by proving an all-level factorization formula for Selberg averages of generalized Jack polynomials. Taking a coefficientwise Jack limit of the generalized Macdonald Pieri rule, we obtain the required one-box matrix elements in the strict Cauchy dual basis. A rational corner-function identity then evaluates the sum over all parent double partitions, while an explicit total derivative of the Selberg kernel yields a triangular recursion on the Dotsenko-Fateev charge balance hyperplane. The unique solution of this recursion is the generalized Kadell formula previously verified only through finite level. Combining this result with the generalized Cauchy identity identifies each double partition term with the corresponding Nekrasov fixed-point contribution.

AI.tldr: The paper proves the full all-level four-point SU(2) AGT correspondence with four fundamental hypermultiplets at generic β, by establishing an all-level factorization formula for Selberg averages of generalized Jack polynomials and identifying each double partition term with Nekrasov fixed-point contributions.
AI.motivation: To provide a complete proof of the AGT correspondence for the four-point SU(2) case with four fundamental hypermultiplets at generic deformation parameter β, extending previous finite-level verifications to all levels.
AI.method: The proof uses: (1) a coefficientwise Jack limit of the generalized Macdonald Pieri rule to obtain one-box matrix elements in the strict Cauchy dual basis; (2) a rational corner-function identity to evaluate sums over parent double partitions; (3) an explicit total derivative of the Selberg kernel yielding a triangular recursion on the Dotsenko-Fateev charge balance hyperplane; (4) combining the resulting generalized Kadell formula with the generalized Cauchy identity to match double partition terms with Nekrasov fixed-point contributions.
AI.result: An all-level factorization formula for Selberg averages of generalized Jack polynomials is proven, yielding the generalized Kadell formula as the unique solution of a triangular recursion, establishing the full four-point SU(2) AGT correspondence at generic β.
AI.conclusion: The all-level AGT correspondence is rigorously established for the four-point SU(2) case with four fundamental hypermultiplets, with the generalized Kadell formula now proven at all levels rather than only verified at finite level.

title: Learning Transverse Momentum Distributions from Raw Scattering Events via Conditional Diffusion
comment: Accepted at Physics and AI at Stanford University (PAI 2026)
summary: Extracting transverse momentum dependent parton distribution functions (TMD PDFs) from semi-inclusive deep inelastic scattering (SIDIS) data is a central goal of the nucleon structure program at Jefferson Lab and the future Electron-Ion Collider. Traditional extraction methods rely on parameterized functional forms and iterative fitting, which can limit the flexibility of the resulting distributions and make uncertainty quantification cumbersome. We present a conditional diffusion model that learns to map raw SIDIS event kinematics directly to TMD PDFs, bypassing explicit functional assumptions. Evaluated on simulated SIDIS data at CLAS12 kinematics, the model recovers the underlying TMD with informative uncertainties that narrow steadily with increasing event statistics, and produces reliable estimates even with as few as 1,000 conditioning events, a statistics-limited regime directly relevant to ongoing and planned experiments.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a conditional diffusion model that directly maps raw SIDIS event kinematics to transverse momentum dependent parton distribution functions (TMD PDFs), bypassing traditional parameterized functional forms and iterative fitting approaches.
AI.motivation: Traditional TMD PDF extraction methods rely on parameterized functional forms and iterative fitting, which limit flexibility of resulting distributions and make uncertainty quantification cumbersome. A more flexible, data-driven approach is needed.
AI.method: A conditional diffusion model is trained to learn a direct mapping from raw SIDIS event kinematics to TMD PDFs, eliminating explicit functional assumptions about the underlying distributions.
AI.result: On simulated SIDIS data at CLAS12 kinematics, the model recovers the underlying TMD with informative uncertainties that narrow with increasing event statistics. It produces reliable estimates even with as few as 1,000 conditioning events.
AI.conclusion: The conditional diffusion approach provides a flexible, statistics-efficient framework for TMD PDF extraction, demonstrating viability in the low-statistics regime directly relevant to ongoing and planned experiments at Jefferson Lab and the future Electron-Ion Collider.

title: Too good to go: Upcycling Phase-Space Points for Multijet Processes
summary: The efficient sampling of high-dimensional phase spaces is a major challenge for Monte Carlo event generators, as for high-multiplicity final states the evaluation of scattering matrix elements becomes computationally expensive. We here introduce a training strategy that significantly reduces the cost of adapting the samplers, while delivering samplers that outperform the current benchmarks. The method exploits the nested structure of phase spaces, where an $(N+1)$-particle phase space factorises into an $N$-particle and a one-particle phase space. We thereby assume that an efficient sampler for the corresponding $N$-particle phase space is already available, as is the case in stacks of QCD $X+n$-jets processes. By augmenting an $N$-particle to an $(N+1)$-particle dataset, we obtain a training sample that more closely resembles the integrand and is statistically larger than, for example, a uniformly sampled one. Starting the adaptation phase of the sampler with a well-sampled $N$-particle core accelerates learning of the full $(N+1)$-particle phase-space density. Since the augmented sample is only used as an initial proposal distribution, unbiased Monte Carlo estimates are still guaranteed by exact event weighting. The approach is agnostic to the trained sampler and can be applied to machine-learning-based methods as well as more traditional algorithms such as VEGAS. We demonstrate the reduction in matrix-element evaluations and final performance increase for jet-associated Drell--Yan and top-pair production at the LHC, using Continuous Normalising Flow samplers.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a training strategy for Monte Carlo event generators that exploits the nested (factorized) structure of phase spaces, using an existing N-particle sampler to augment and seed the training of an (N+1)-particle sampler. This reduces adaptation cost and improves sampler performance, demonstrated with Continuous Normalizing Flows for Drell-Yan and top-pair production at the LHC, while remaining unbiased through exact event weighting.
AI.motivation: Efficient sampling of high-dimensional phase spaces is a major challenge for Monte Carlo event generators because evaluating scattering matrix elements for high-multiplicity final states is computationally expensive. Existing sampler training approaches are costly and suboptimal for high-dimensional settings.
AI.method: The method leverages the factorization of (N+1)-particle phase spaces into an N-particle and a one-particle phase space. Given an existing efficient N-particle sampler (e.g., in the stack of QCD X+n-jet processes), the authors augment N-particle samples to construct an (N+1)-particle training dataset that more closely resembles the integrand and is statistically larger than uniform sampling. This augmented sample seeds the adaptation phase of the (N+1)-particle sampler, accelerating learning. Since the augmented sample serves only as an initial proposal, exact event weighting guarantees unbiased Monte Carlo estimates. The approach is agnostic to the sampler type (machine-learning-based or traditional like VEGAS).
AI.result: The method reduces the number of matrix-element evaluations required for adaptation and improves the final performance of the samplers, demonstrated for jet-associated Drell-Yan and top-pair production at the LHC using Continuous Normalizing Flow samplers.
AI.conclusion: Exploiting the nested structure of phase spaces provides a general, sampler-agnostic strategy to reduce training cost and improve sampler quality in Monte Carlo event generation, with unbiased estimates preserved through exact event weighting.

title: Exploring $Z/γ$-mediated heavy FCNCs at the FCC-ee
summary: The flavor structure of the Standard Model (SM) remains one of the most compelling questions in particle physics, with the third generation being particularly intriguing due to its significantly larger masses and comparatively less precisely measured properties. These features make third-generation flavor transitions particularly interesting in context of search for physics beyond the SM. In this work, we investigate flavor-violating transitions between the third and the first two generations, mediated by the neutral gauge bosons ($Z/γ$), within the framework of the SM Effective Field Theory (SMEFT), using dipole and Higgs-current operators. We determine the optimal sensitivities using the optimal observable technique (OOT) at different center-of-mass energies of the upcoming Future Circular Collider in the $e^+e^-$ mode (FCC-ee). We further derive complementary constraints on the relevant SMEFT operators from low-energy flavor-violating observables and heavy fermion decay channels. Our analysis also reveals characteristic interference patterns among the dipole contributions, which depend on the underlying flavor transition and exhibit distinct behavior between the $Z$ pole and higher-energy FCC-ee stages. The FCC-ee provides a complementary and direct probe of flavor-violating interactions at the electroweak scale, with the projections showing improved sensitivity for several interactions and comparable sensitivity to existing flavor constraints for several others. This highlights the importance of a systematic assessment across the different FCC-ee energy stages, which provides a comprehensive picture of its potential to explore flavor-violating phenomena and its complementarity with low-energy flavor experiments.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates flavor-violating transitions between the third and first two generations via neutral gauge bosons (Z/γ) within the SMEFT framework, using the optimal observable technique to determine sensitivities at different FCC-ee center-of-mass energies. It derives complementary constraints from low-energy flavor observables and heavy fermion decays, revealing characteristic interference patterns among dipole contributions and demonstrating FCC-ee's complementary and improved sensitivity for probing flavor-violating interactions at the electroweak scale.
AI.motivation: The third generation of the Standard Model has significantly larger masses and less precisely measured properties, making third-generation flavor transitions particularly interesting for probing physics beyond the SM. The authors aim to systematically assess the potential of FCC-ee to explore these flavor-violating phenomena.
AI.method: The study employs the Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT) framework with dipole and Higgs-current operators, applies the optimal observable technique (OOT) to determine optimal sensitivities at different FCC-ee center-of-mass energies, and derives complementary constraints from low-energy flavor-violating observables and heavy fermion decay channels.

FCC-ee projections show improved sensitivity for several interactions and comparable sensitivity to existing flavor constraints for others.
AI.conclusion: FCC-ee provides a complementary and direct probe of flavor-violating interactions at the electroweak scale, and a systematic assessment across different FCC-ee energy stages is essential to comprehensively evaluate its potential for exploring flavor-violating phenomena in complementarity with low-energy flavor experiments.

title: Chiral soliton lattice in inhomogeneous magnetic fields
summary: It has been known that in sufficiently strong uniform magnetic fields, the ground state of quantum chromodynamics (QCD) supports a spatially modulated condensate of neutral pions, dubbed chiral soliton lattice (CSL). In this paper, we investigate whether a similar ordered ground state might exist when the external magnetic field is nonuniform, as appropriate for potential phenomenological applications, including heavy-ion collisions and neutron stars. To that end, we use the low-energy effective field theory of QCD, restricted to the neutral pions as the sole low-energy degrees of freedom in strong magnetic fields. In the limit of vanishing pion mass, we achieve a complete characterization of magnetic fields supporting a CSL-like ground state. Moreover, for a simple but infinite family of magnetic fields, we find the corresponding CSL state analytically. Going away from the massless limit requires full numerical minimization of the energy functional. Here we provide some sample numerical results, focusing on the qualitative differences as compared to the situations with a uniform magnetic field or a vanishing pion mass. The main conclusion remains unchanged: while bending the magnetic field typically reduces the energy gain due to the neutral pion condensation, a CSL-type ground state is still possible. As a byproduct of our work, we map the location of the CSL phase in the phase diagram of QCD in a uniform magnetic field and finite volume.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates whether chiral soliton lattice (CSL) ground states of QCD, previously known to exist in strong uniform magnetic fields, persist when the magnetic field is nonuniform, using low-energy effective field theory with neutral pions as the only degrees of freedom.
AI.motivation: To determine if a CSL-like ordered ground state exists under nonuniform magnetic fields, which are more relevant for phenomenological applications such as heavy-ion collisions and neutron stars, rather than only in idealized uniform fields.
AI.method: Uses low-energy effective field theory (EFT) of QCD restricted to neutral pion degrees of freedom. In the massless pion limit, provides a complete characterization of magnetic fields supporting CSL ground states and finds analytic solutions for an infinite family of magnetic field configurations. For massive pions, performs full numerical minimization of the energy functional.
AI.result: Analytic solutions for CSL states are found for an infinite family of nonuniform magnetic fields in the massless limit. Numerical results show that bending the magnetic field typically reduces the energy gain from neutral pion condensation, but a CSL-type ground state remains possible. The paper also maps the CSL phase location in the QCD phase diagram for uniform magnetic fields at finite volume.
AI.conclusion: CSL-type ground states persist even under nonuniform magnetic fields, although the energy gain is generally reduced by field bending. This extends the validity of the CSL phenomenon to more realistic conditions relevant for heavy-ion collisions and neutron stars. A byproduct is the finite-volume phase diagram mapping of CSL in uniform fields.

title: Enigmatic properties of $Ξ(1620)$ and $Ξ(1690)$
summary: Motivated by a considerable release of data on first two excited states of the doubly strange baryon, $Ξ(1620)$ and $Ξ(1690)$, from different experimental collaborations in recent years, we investigate meson-baryon interactions in a coupled-channel approach. The systems are composed of pseudoscalar and vector mesons and the calculations are done for the total spin 1/2 and isospin 1/2 configuration. The tree-level interactions are deduced from Lagrangians based on chiral and hidden local symmetries. Specifically, we make an attempt to describe (1) data on the $K^-Λ$ femtoscopic correlation function coming from $p\,p$ and $Pb\,Pb$ collisions, and (2) the available data on invariant mass distributions for different systems: $πΞ$, $\bar K Σ$ and $\bar K Λ$. We find that the amplitude which yields the correlation function close to the data results in mass distributions of different meson-baryon systems that are in discordance with the experimental data and vice-versa.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates meson-baryon interactions in a coupled-channel approach to describe the doubly strange baryon excited states Ξ(1620) and Ξ(1690), using Lagrangians based on chiral and hidden local symmetries. The authors attempt to simultaneously describe K⁻Λ femtoscopic correlation function data and invariant mass distributions for πΞ, K̄Σ, and K̄Λ systems, but find that these two sets of data cannot be simultaneously reproduced by a single amplitude.
AI.motivation: Recent experimental releases of data on the first two excited states of the doubly strange baryon Ξ(1620) and Ξ(1690) motivate a theoretical investigation of meson-baryon interactions in the coupled-channel framework to understand these resonances and their production/decay mechanisms.
AI.method: A coupled-channel approach is used for systems composed of pseudoscalar and vector mesons with total spin 1/2 and isospin 1/2. Tree-level interactions are derived from Lagrangians based on chiral and hidden local symmetries. The model is used to compute K⁻Λ femtoscopic correlation functions and invariant mass distributions for various meson-baryon systems.
AI.result: The amplitude that reproduces the K⁻Λ femtoscopic correlation function close to the data yields invariant mass distributions for the meson-baryon systems (πΞ, K̄Σ, K̄Λ) that disagree with experimental data, and vice versa — the two observables cannot be simultaneously described by the same amplitude.
AI.conclusion: There is a discordance between the amplitudes needed to describe femtoscopic correlation function data versus invariant mass distribution data, indicating a tension that needs to be resolved for a consistent understanding of the Ξ(1620) and Ξ(1690) resonances in the coupled-channel approach.

title: Hunting long-lived doubly charged scalars at the HL-LHC
summary: This work studies the collider phenomenology of long-lived doubly charged scalars. After reviewing the existing searches for the doubly charged scalar in both the prompt and the long-lived regimes, we identify an intermediate range of proper decay length, namely, $\mathcal{O}(0.1~\mathrm{mm}) \lesssim cτ\lesssim \mathcal{O}(100~\mathrm{mm})$, where conventional searches lose sensitivity. We investigate the prospects for probing the doubly charged scalar both in the presence and in the absence of the $ΔL=2$ Yukawa coupling of the $SU(2)_{L}$ complex triplet. In the presence of this coupling, $H^{\pm\pm}$ can be long-lived only for masses in the range $100$-$150~\mathrm{GeV}$, whereas in the fermiophobic scenario (i.e., in the absence of the $ΔL=2$ coupling), the range extends to $\mathrm{TeV}$ scale. We propose a displaced-vertex search at the HL-LHC for doubly charged scalars with masses up to $\approx 1~\mathrm{TeV}$ and $cτ=10$-$100~\mathrm{mm}$ in the fermiophobic scenario, while a benchmark point with a doubly charged scalar of mass $120~\mathrm{GeV}$ and $cτ= 5~\mathrm{mm}$ is considered when the complex triplet scalar couples to leptons. We show that a cut on the invariant mass of the displaced vertex as reconstructed from the associated tracks can strongly suppress Standard Model backgrounds. We present projected limits on the Drell-Yan pair-production cross section for the doubly charged scalar at $\sqrt{s}=14~\mathrm{TeV}$ with an integrated luminosity of $3000~\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$, considering two illustrative assumptions for the residual background. Displaced-vertex searches thus probe a region complementary to those covered by prompt and heavy stable charged-particle searches.

title: An Axial $U_A(1)_{L_μ-L_τ}$: UV Completion and Experimental Searches
summary: We propose an anomaly-free and renormalizable axial $U_A(1)_{L_μ-L_τ}$ model and study its experimental signatures for $A'$ masses from the MeV scale to the TeV scale. The opposite charges of the left- and right-handed charged leptons forbid the usual muon and tau Yukawa interactions. Their masses are instead generated by a singlet scalar and heavy vector-like leptons through a universal-seesaw mechanism. We focus on heavy vector-like leptons, small light--heavy mixing, and $m_s\gtrsim10~\mathrm{GeV}$. In this limit, the observables considered here depend mainly on $(m_{A'},g_X)$, while the other model parameters are restricted by mixing and perturbativity. We confront this benchmark with current experimental searches. For neutrino trident production, our finite-$m_μ$ calculation shows that $A'$ modifies the axial weak coefficient, rather than the vector coefficient relevant to the usual $L_μ-L_τ$ model. The longitudinal mode enhances muon bremsstrahlung and gives a negative contribution to $(g-2)_μ$; the latter dominates over the scalar contribution in our benchmark. Combining these results with invisible meson decays and four-muon resonance searches, we summarize the phenomenological constraints in the $(m_{A'},g_X)$ plane. For $m_{A'}\gg m_μ$, vector and axial final-state-radiation rates become nearly identical, so the corresponding collider limits can be obtained by rate matching. At a future muon collider, the total rate alone does not fully resolve the interaction structure, whereas angular distributions, especially the forward--backward asymmetry in $μ^+μ^-\toτ^+τ^-$, retain direct sensitivity to chirality.
